# package bridge

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/l2/bridge"
```

Package bridge is the switch of a multiport device: a learning Ethernet bridge between its physical ports, with the device's interface attached as one more port (the "CPU port").

Frames are classified by their destination address:

  - Link-local frames (01-80-C2-00-00-00 to -0F: LLDP, PTCP delay) and MRP frames (01-15-4E-00-00-01 to -04) belong to the port they arrived on: they reach that port's local [l2.Port](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/l2#Port) ([Bridge.Port](#func-bridge-port)) and are never forwarded. What the device sends on a local port leaves on that port only, whatever its state: the LLDP agent and the MRP entity of each port use these.
  - Frames to the interface's MAC address reach the CPU port ([Bridge.CPU](#func-bridge-cpu)); broadcast and other multicast frames reach it and are flooded to the other forwarding ports; other unicast frames go to the port their destination was learned on, or are flooded.
  - What the device sends on the CPU port goes to the port its destination was learned on, or is flooded to every forwarding port.

A port is forwarding or blocked ([Bridge.SetState](#func-bridge-setstate)): a blocked port carries only its local frames, as a ring port that MRP blocks. A port can also be a boundary for multicast groups ([Bridge.SetBoundary](#func-bridge-setboundary)): frames to those groups are neither forwarded to nor from it; they still reach the CPU port.

The forwarding database is bounded: when it is full new stations are not learned (their frames are flooded). Entries age out, and [Bridge.Flush](#func-bridge-flush) forgets them all, as MRP topology changes demand. Nothing here is hardware switching: forwarding takes a goroutine hop and a copy per frame, so the bridge suits tests and software devices, not deterministic real-time forwarding.

#### func New

```go
func New(cfg Config) (*Bridge, error)
```

New starts a bridge over cfg.Ports. Close stops it; it does not close the physical ports.

#### func (Bridge) CPU

```go
func (b *Bridge) CPU() l2.Port
```

CPU returns the interface's port: build the device's [l2.Mux](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/l2#Mux) on it.

#### func (Bridge) Close

```go
func (b *Bridge) Close() error
```

Close stops the bridge: the CPU and local ports report profinet.ErrClosed. The physical ports stay open.

#### func (Bridge) Flush

```go

```

Flush forgets every learned station.

#### func (Bridge) Port

```go
func (b *Bridge) Port(i int) l2.Port
```

Port returns the local port of physical port i (0-based): its link-local and MRP frames, and a way to send on that port alone. It reports the physical port's MAC address and link state.

#### func (Bridge) SetBlocked

```go
func (b *Bridge) SetBlocked(i int, blocked bool)
```

SetBlocked blocks port i (0-based) or makes it forward; the MRP entity (package mrp) uses it.

#### func (Bridge) SetBoundary

```go
func (b *Bridge) SetBoundary(i int, groups []ethernet.MAC)
```

SetBoundary makes port i (0-based) a boundary for the given multicast groups: frames to them are not forwarded to or from it. nil clears it.

#### func (Bridge) SetState

```go
func (b *Bridge) SetState(i int, s State)
```

SetState sets the forwarding state of port i (0-based). Blocking a port forgets the stations learned on it.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Ports are the physical ports, port 1 first; at least one. A bridge
	// forwards what is not addressed to it, so each port must receive
	// every frame on its link: promiscuous, without a multicast filter (a
	// vnet endpoint with Promiscuous set, a raw socket in promiscuous
	// mode).
	Ports []l2.Port
	// MAC is the interface's MAC address, the address of the CPU port;
	// required, and distinct from the ports' addresses.
	MAC ethernet.MAC
	// QueueLen is the receive queue of the CPU port and of every local
	// port; zero means DefaultQueueLen. A full queue drops the frame.
	QueueLen int
	// AgeTime is how long a learned station is kept without a frame from
	// it; zero means DefaultAgeTime.
	AgeTime time.Duration
	// MaxFDB bounds the forwarding database; zero means DefaultMaxFDB.
	MaxFDB int
	// Logger receives diagnostics; nil logs nothing.
	Logger profinet.Logger
}
```

Config configures a bridge.

### type PortStats

```go
type PortStats struct {
	Received  uint64 // frames read from the port
	Sent      uint64 // frames written to the port
	Local     uint64 // received frames delivered to the local port
	Forwarded uint64 // received frames forwarded to other ports
	Dropped   uint64 // received frames dropped (blocked, boundary, full queue)
	SendErrs  uint64 // writes that failed
}
```

PortStats are the counters of a physical port.
